about: Per-case provenance for experiments/adversarial_probes.py: what each finding is measured against (docstring, repo rule, independent truth, the function's own output) and how strongly. Written after the run; the pre-registered class is kept in the run file as 'class', the revised one as 'audited_class'.
revision_basis: post-hoc, by the same author who wrote the predictions; the reasons are in each note and the run file keeps both

strengths.DIRECT: text applies to this object as written
strengths.ANALOGY: text applies by extension; maintainers may read it otherwise
strengths.EXTERNAL: standard outside the repo, quoted from the source on the stated date
strengths.COMPUTED: a value computed in this audit, not a quotation

basis.quote: Returns the verdict "pass" or "fail" with the residual L3 - (L1 + L2).

basis.source: three-distance theorem as stated in the docstring: L3 = L1 + L2; scale-free

A01.note: Docstring says nothing about whether tol is absolute or relative. The output carries tol and residual, so the reading is not hidden (CLAUDE.md bounds rule is met). Callers use lengths of order 1 (window_extent.py:102, three_gap_check.py:61). Prereg class DEFECT revised to LIMIT: no docstring or repo rule is contradicted; the independent truth (scale invariance) shows the absolute tolerance is a unit-dependent instrument bound.

basis.quote: Returns the verdict "pass" or "fail" with the residual L3 - (L1 + L2).

A02.note: At 1e12 scale one float step is 4.9e-4, so the residual 4.9e-4 is one rounding step, not a failure of the theorem. Same reading as A01; the output records residual and tol. Prereg DEFECT revised to LIMIT.

basis.quote: Consistency check on a set of distinct gap lengths.

A03.note: [1,1,2] is not a set of distinct lengths, so it is outside the docstring's stated input. NaN input: docstring silent. Class unchanged.

basis.quote: keep every requested output
A slot with nothing in it stays void (null), never dropped and never filled to look complete.

A04.note: angle_histogram has no docstring. Whether an angle outside [lo, hi] is a 'requested output' is a reading of the rule, not its text. Only caller (toolkit/generator.py:90, width 15, hi 360) is fed angles in [0, 360), so no stored run is affected. Prereg DEFECT revised to UNDEFINED with a conflict-by-analogy flag; the omission of any count of dropped angles is the part that matches the bounds rule's 'unknown ... not omitted' wording only by analogy.

A05.note: Computed here: angle_histogram([181.0], width=7.0, lo=0.0, hi=180.0) returns hi = 180.0 and 26 bins, the last covering [175, 182), and counts 181. The function's own output states a range its bins exceed, and its own branch 'elif a == hi' shows hi was meant to be the last edge. No docstring, no repo rule needed: the returned record disagrees with itself. Only for widths that do not divide hi - lo; the one caller uses 15 on 360.

basis.source: the direction of the zero vector is undefined; atan2(0, 0) = 0.0 is a convention, not a direction

basis.quote: A slot with nothing in it stays void (null), never dropped and never filled to look complete.

A06.note: Two parts. (a) A point at the centroid is returned with direction 0.0, indistinguishable from a real 0 degree point (undefined; no spec). (b) (-1e-15 deg) % 360.0 evaluates to 360.0 in float arithmetic, outside [0, 360); the one caller maps 360.0 into the last histogram bin through the 'a == hi' branch. Prereg DEFECT revised to UNDEFINED: no docstring exists and the rule applies only by analogy.

basis.quote: List of k in 2..k_max such that rotating by 360/k maps the set to itself.
The bound rotational_symmetry reads at, for the same arguments.
any count / period / symmetry reading logs the instrument bound it was read at (points, precision, probe step); unknown bound = void, not omitted.

A07.note: Read literally, the docstring is contradicted (the 3-point cluster is not mapped to itself). But rel_tol is in the signature and the bound line logs abs_tol = 1.000000004553418 for this set, as the bounds rule asks; degeneracy() on the same set reports coincident = True, central = True, n_at_centre = 3 at tol 1e-6. The repo already reports that the tolerance exceeds the cluster. Prereg DEFECT revised to LIMIT. What a reader sees only if they call the bound or degeneracy probe is not in the symmetry list itself.

A08.note: Reading flips at eps = 1.0104e-6 (rel_tol times scale), as the tolerance parameter says. Unchanged.

A09.note: One-sided: the probe never reports a symmetry the exact matching denies (0 of 20,000 trials). It misses 8 of 46 when one image point lies within tolerance of two source points. Unchanged.

A13.note: Two readings conflict: the docstring says 'the set' (a repeated vertex does not change a set, reading [2,3,6]); the contributing rule says repeated points are retained (multiset reading, [] observed). Neither text decides.

basis.source: Kaspar-Schuster algorithm computed here; 0 mismatches in 3000 random strings plus known values

A15.note: Timing only (n = 20,000 in 0.24 s on the test machine). No spec states a time bound. The prereg prediction was wrong.

A16.note: 'Symbol string' is not defined for multi-character symbols; ['1','10'] and ['11','0'] read identically. Docstring silent. Unchanged.

basis.source: smallest period = n minus the longest proper border, computed here; 0 mismatches in 3000 strings

A17.note: smallest_period has no docstring; truth is the standard border characterisation. Unchanged.

basis.quote: share of gaps that have the rarest of three lengths
None or 0 for the frequency means it is not known

A18.note: The docstring calls the argument a share of gaps (domain 0 to 1) and names only None and 0 as 'not known'. -0.5, 5.0 and NaN are outside the stated domain and are assessed. Unchanged.

basis.quote: Numeric values that cannot be represented in the grammar below (such as Infinity and NaN) are not permitted.
The resulting text MUST strictly conform to the JSON grammar.
nonfinite numbers and duplicate object keys are rejected

A19.note: Defect only against the external standard. The rule 'nonfinite numbers ... are rejected' is in docs/schema.md, which governs the Manus build (explorative_math/, examples/); emlib.write_run belongs to the Claude Code build and no rule there says the same. Seven committed files in runs/ already hold 191 bare +Infinity values (combine_seed0, combine_seed1, combine_small_seed0, fold_loop_seed0, fold_shape_seed0, layered_pursuit_seed0, layered_pursuit_small_seed0), from experiments/fold_loop.py:180, fold_shape.py:199 and layered_pursuit.py:78 mapping None to float('inf'). Python's json.loads reads them; JavaScript JSON.parse and other strict parsers do not. A default change would stop those experiments from rerunning, so the fix proposal is opt-in.
